title: Bound by Fate
author: William Saville
content:
Melanie stood onstage, the applause gradually fading but still ringing in her ears. The open mic night had gone better than she could have hoped! As she stepped off the stage, her heart fluttered with exhilaration. The dimly lit bar was filled with the scent of spilled beer and the faint sweetness of cheap wine. The walls, adorned with faded posters of past performers, echoed the memories of countless artists who had poured their hearts into their songs. As the last chords faded, her boyfriend, Jason, beamed at her from the audience, pride radiating from his smile as he clapped vigorously, his hands creating a rhythm that thrummed with encouragement.

“Great job, Mel! You’re incredible!” he said as she approached, throwing his arms around her and squeezing her lovingly before kissing her tenderly on the lips.

She giggled at him, her heart swelling with affection. The warmth of the room and the buzz of applause wrapped around her like his comforting embrace. But after her performance, she desperately needed nicotine and fresh air.

Pulling her worn, oversized jacket from the chair to ward off the crisp autumn chill outside, she told Jason she would be back in a flash and headed to the back door leading to the alleyway designated for smoking. The night air hit her like a refreshing wave, carrying the scent of damp earth and the faint smoke from distant chimneys. She pulled her jacket around her more tightly. The alley behind the bar was dimly lit, with an old flickering neon sign, and distant streetlights casting erratic shadows that danced along the graffiti-covered walls. She leaned against the cool brick, savoring the brief solitude as she pulled out her vape.

Taking a moment to indulge in the calming strawberry lemonade flavor, she closed her eyes, enjoying the fresh air. A rustle of trash caught her attention, the wind stirring the discarded wrappers and old newspapers piled near a smelly dumpster, the pungent odor mingling with the sweetness of her vape. The faint sound of cars honking in the distance underscored the rhythm of the night.

As she took another puff, the taste of fruit lingered in the back of her throat, but tranquility shattered like glass when a figure emerged from the shadows. A man, tall and imposing, stepped into the dim light, cigarette smoke curling around him like a fog.

“No escape,” he said, his voice low and gravelly, as he suddenly pushed her against the brick wall. The words felt both accusatory and promising.

Melanie’s heart raced. “Please don’t hurt me!” she blurted out, panic bubbling beneath her skin as she tried to free herself.

He stepped closer, a smirk playing on his lips. In a swift movement, he rolled up his sleeve to reveal a tattoo etched in dark ink; her words, tattooed forever on his skin. “Look familiar?” he taunted, his eyes piercing through her.

A chill ran down her spine as the realization sank in. She knew everyone had soulmates marked by fate, each person born with a tattoo that displayed the first words their fated partner would ever say to them, but this was more than mere superstition; it felt like a curse. Melanie had always known her soulmate would be dangerous. "No Escape" was her tattoo, and nothing could be more ominous or creepy.

“Who… who are you?” she whispered, her voice trembling.

“Aaron,” he replied, stepping even closer, his presence overwhelming. The air crackled with an electric tension, an unspoken understanding igniting between them. "What's your name, soulmate?"

She looked down, her voice barely a whisper. “Melanie.”

“The fates claimed us, bound us in their grasp,” he said, his tone shifting from playful to serious. “We’re not just soulmates; we’re two halves of a shattered mirror, forever reflecting our pain.”

Every word he spoke sent tremors through her. She felt an undeniable pull toward him, a magnetic force that made her heart race. He leaned in, his fingers gently gripping her chin, tilting her face up to meet his gaze. The kiss he pressed to her lips ignited a storm inside her, a wildfire of passion that consumed all thought of Jason, of her past life.

In that moment, everything changed. All the love she had known, every promise made, dissolved into nothingness, leaving only the intoxicating heat of his touch.

Aaron pulled away, his eyes dark with intensity. “I’ve been watching you sing. I didn't even know who you were yet, but I knew I had to have you.” He flashed a sly grin. “I’m in a band. And now that I know you're my soulmate, you’ll have to sing for me. Everything you do will be for me.”

Her heart raced as she processed his words. Standing there in the alley, she felt her previous life slipping away like sand through her fingers. Jason, her dreams, her independence; all eclipsed by this new connection. The joy of singing that once filled her with light now felt tainted, overshadowed by the weight of this destiny.

The cool autumn breeze picked up, swirling around them and causing her to shiver. She pulled her jacket tighter around her shoulders, trying to stave off the chill. Kissing him again, she felt a rush of conflicting emotions wash over her; hope, despair, exhilaration, and fear. She wouldn’t be alone anymore, but this man before her, whose presence ignited a whirlwind of emotions, was shrouded in shadows. She was tethered to him by a thread of fate that could only lead to heartache.

“Are you ready for this, Melanie?” Aaron murmured, his voice low and intimate, echoing the weight of his promise. “Because once you step into my world, there’s no going back.”

She met his gaze, a mixture of dread and longing swirling within her. The darkness beckoned, and she felt the pull of destiny tightening around her like a noose. This was the choice she never made, the path laid out by forces beyond her control.

With a deep breath, she whispered, “I’m ready.”

As the words left her lips, the flickering streetlight above them buzzed ominously, casting eerie shadows across their faces. The alleyway, filled with the scent of dampness and a hint of danger, became their stage; a place where fate had woven their lives together. The distant sounds of laughter and music faded, swallowed by the darkness, leaving only the two of them standing at the precipice of an unknown future.

In that moment, she understood that in this endless dance, there was no escape.
